sections.h2: Estate tax and inheritance tax in Idaho
sections.html:
Idaho collects no estate tax or inheritance tax today. It has no gift tax either, and its estate tax expired in 2004. The estate tax rules still on file apply only to deaths before January 1, 2005.

An heir selling an Idaho house therefore owes no state death tax on the transfer itself. The State Tax Commission takes questions about deaths before 2005 at (208) 334-7660 in the Boise area and (800) 972-7660 toll-free.

Other taxes can still reach an inherited house. Very large estates face federal estate tax, a sale can create income tax on a gain, and the property tax bill keeps coming while the estate is open.

sections.h2: When the federal estate tax applies
sections.html:
Federal estate tax matters only when an estate tops the basic exclusion amount, set at $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026. A federal return is required at that same figure for the year of death.

Federal estate and gift figures for 2026
MeasureAmount (2026)
Basic exclusion amount$15,000,000
Estate tax filing threshold$15,000,000
Annual gift exclusion per donee$19,000

Confirm the amount for the year of death, since the figure is set by federal law and can change.

The test looks at the whole estate, not the house alone. An executor totals real estate, bank and brokerage accounts, business interests and other assets to decide whether a federal return is due. Most Idaho families fall well below the line.

sections.h2: An heir's basis when an Idaho house is sold
sections.html:
For tax purposes the heir's starting cost is usually the home's market value on the day the owner died (IRS Publication 551). Any gain is counted from that figure, and what the original owner paid long ago drops out.

  • A quick sale near the date-of-death value leaves little gain.
  • Holding the house while prices climb makes the rise above that value taxable.
  • A different rule can apply when the decedent was given the property within a year before death.
  • An appraisal dated to the day of death backs up the figure.

When the house later sells, our Idaho capital gains guide covers the state's 60% deduction for real property held 12 months. A tax professional can say how that 12-month clock runs for inherited property.

sections.h2: Who can sell an inherited house?
sections.html:
Only the court-appointed personal representative can sign a sale. Under Idaho Code 15-3-711 the representative holds the same control over title that an absolute owner has, as a trustee for those entitled to the estate, and section 15-3-715 lists authorized transactions, including selling, mortgaging or leasing real or personal property of the estate.

The same section lets the representative:

  • dispose of land, in Idaho or another state, for cash or on credit, at public or private sale;
  • make ordinary or extraordinary repairs to buildings;
  • pay taxes, assessments and the costs of administration;
  • hire attorneys, auditors or agents to help.

A will or court order can narrow these powers, so a will that restricts sale changes the answer. Buyers get some cover from Idaho Code 15-3-714: a limit on the representative's power binds only people who actually knew about it.

Idaho Code 15-3-1201 lets a successor collect certain assets by affidavit when the probate estate is worth $100,000 or less. It works once 30 days have elapsed since the death, and only if no petition for a personal representative is pending or granted anywhere.

The affidavit route reaches payment of debts, tangible personal property, instruments of debt and securities. Real estate is absent from that list, so a house is not clearly within this shortcut. Ask the title company what it needs to close, and see a probate attorney if the estate is under the threshold but holds real property.

The affidavit must state that the fair market value of the entire estate subject to probate, less liens and encumbrances, is no more than $100,000. The Department of Health and Welfare is treated as a successor for medical assistance recovery in some cases, under subsection (c). Our Idaho probate guide explains the court route in full.

sections.h2: Idaho statutes that govern an estate sale
sections.html:
Estate administration lives in Title 15, Chapter 3 of the Idaho Code, the Uniform Probate Code chapter on wills and administration. Five of its parts bear on a house sale.

  • Part 7: duties and powers of personal representatives.
  • Part 10: closing estates.
  • Part 11: compromise of controversies.
  • Part 12: collection of personal property by affidavit and summary procedure for small estates.
  • Part 13: uniform estate tax apportionment.

Part 13 only divides estate tax among recipients. It creates no state tax. Parts 7 and 10 do the most work in a sale: Part 7 sets what the representative may do, and Part 10 covers wrapping up the estate once the house has closed.

A gift during life raises a different question. Idaho has no gift tax, and the federal annual exclusion is $19,000 per recipient for 2026. A gift of real estate worth more than that amount is a federal question to raise with a tax professional. Our Idaho quitclaim deed guide covers the deed itself.

sections.h2: Costs while the house is unsold
sections.html:
From the date of death until closing, the estate carries the property tax, insurance and upkeep. Counties treat the estate like any other owner. Take Ada County: the first half falls due December 20 and the second half June 20, and a late payment draws a 2% charge plus monthly interest.

The personal representative may pay taxes and administration expenses out of estate funds under section 15-3-715. The homeowner's exemption runs until ownership changes or the home stops being a primary residence. Ask the county Assessor if it carries on after a death.

Our Idaho property tax guide and the county guides for Ada and Canyon list the assessor and treasurer offices.

Timing matters for the carrying costs. Each month the house stays unsold adds another round of utilities and insurance, so ask the title company early how long it expects to need once the court has confirmed the representative's authority.

A vacant inherited house keeps running up tax, utility and insurance bills, and any will restriction or court order must be settled before a sale.

We buy houses as is in Idaho, including inherited ones, so cleanout and repairs do not need to come first. Call or text for a written cash offer, and if you decline it you owe us nothing. Before you accept any offer, confirm the personal representative holds the authority described above and that an attorney has looked over the estate papers.

Pull together the death certificate, the court letters, the deed and the newest property tax bill before talking to any buyer. A title company asks about those four items first.

faqs.q: Does Idaho have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. Idaho has no gift tax or inheritance tax, and its estate tax expired in 2004.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax when I inherit a house in Idaho?
faqs.a: Idaho does not tax the inheritance itself. You may owe income tax on a gain if you later sell for more than the date-of-death value.

faqs.q: What is the federal estate tax exemption for 2026?
faqs.a: The basic exclusion amount is $15,000,000 for people who die in 2026, and the filing threshold is the same.

faqs.q: Can a personal representative sell real estate without court approval?
faqs.a: Idaho Code 15-3-715 lets a personal representative sell estate real property unless the will or a court order restricts it, so check both.

faqs.q: Is a small estate affidavit enough to sell a house?
faqs.a: Probably not. Idaho Code 15-3-1201 covers payment of debts, tangible personal property, instruments and securities for estates of $100,000 or less, and real estate is absent from that list.
